request.query: Opening a bank account in Finland without a Finnish personal identity code, experiences
request.objective: Find bank pages, forum threads and expat guides about opening a Finnish bank account without a personal identity code. Rank bank requirement pages (OP, Nordea, S-Pankki) and first-hand experiences first. Pull sentences on what each bank requires.

results.title: Survey of the availability of banking services to foreign persons moving to Finland
results.author: Anu Kettunen
highlights:
As its interpretation, the FIN-FSA states that the definition of legally resident in an EEA member state is fulfilled at least in circumstances where a person arriving to Finland demonstrates they have applied for asylum or a temporary protection permit from Finland. The obligation to provide basic banking services commences already when the application is pending. According to the FIN-FSA’s interpretation, in circumstances where moving to Finland requires another residence permit, basic banking services must be provider already while the residence permit application is pending at least in circumstances where the person is already living in Finland by virtue of the pending residence permit application. Also in circumstances where the bank considers it has no obligation to provide basic banking services to a customer in the process of moving to Finland since the customer is not yet by definition residing in an EEA member state, the bank may, at its discretion, open banking services for the customer insofar as the identity of the customer can be verified and other regulatory anti-money laundering obligations can be proportionately fulfilled. The FIN-FSA highlights the importance of financial inclusion and the equal and non-discriminatory treatment of customers in the provision of banking services. The availability of banking services and the commencement of service provision to foreigners moving to Finland should not restricted solely to circumstance where the bank is under a statutory obligation to provide basic banking services. 4.2.2 Requiring a Finnish personal identity code A bank may refuse to provide basic banking services only for a reason based on law. In the context of the survey, it was discovered that at least one bank requires a Finnish personal identity code in order to open basic banking services. The FIN-FSA states that the lack of a Finnish personal identity code is not a statutory reason to deprive a customer of basic banking services, with the exception of granting a strong electronic means of identification. 10 The requirement of a Finnish personal identity code in the provision of other services defined as basic banking services must stop without delay.

...

Memorandum 10 (11) 
11 September 2023 
BOF/FIN-FSA-CONFIDENTIAL 
Public 
4.2.3 Verification of the customer’s identity and due diligence information as prerequisites 
for the provision of basic banking services 
The opening of a bank account is contingent on the bank being able to 
identify and know the customer in accordance with the provisions of the 
AML Act. 
As stated in section 3.1.3, with respect to customers without a Finnish 
personal identity code, the AML Act requires that the customer’s travel 
document information is also retained as customer due diligence 
information. Banks typically accept a passport, or with respect to 
Schengen countries’ citizens, an identity card as a travel document. 
In particular, as regards asylum seekers entering the country without a 
valid passport, the requirement of a travel document could lead to a 
situation where no banking services could be provided due to 
deficiencies related to due diligence information under the AML Act. 
The FIN-FSA acknowledges the problem in regulation and welcomes a 
clarification to legislation to realise the right of access to basic banking 
services as intended in regulation for all asylum seekers entering the 
country legally. 
As regards the collection of customer due diligence information, the 
FIN-FSA recommends that banks would not require the submission of 
unreasonably extensive information so as not to deprive customers of 
access to basic banking services where they have the statutory right to 
use these services.

results.title: Opening a Finnish Bank Account Before You Have a Henkilötunnus | NordicExpat
results.author: Bikram Nath
highlights:
1. Set up an interim international account first. Before you so much as call a Finnish bank, open an account you can use immediately (more on this below). This removes the panic of needing money to move today and lets you negotiate the Finnish account calmly.
2. Gather your documents. Passport or EEA ID, residence permit or registration certificate, and your Finnish address details.
3. Pick a bank and book an in-person appointment. The major retail banks are Nordea, OP, S-Pankki and Danske Bank. Most have a newcomer page and an English-language phone line. Account opening in Finland almost always involves an appointment rather than a fully online flow for non-residents.
4. Ask for a basic payment account by name. If the advisor says a henkilötunnus is required, explain that you are asking specifically for peruspankkipalvelut / a basic payment account, which Finanssivalvonta says cannot require a personal identity code as a precondition. Keep it factual and friendly — the person in front of you is following a script, not making policy.
5. Get any refusal in writing. This is your safety net, covered in the next section.
6. Upgrade later. Once DVV assigns your henkilötunnus, go back and add full online banking IDs and strong electronic identification.

results.title: How to open a bank account in Finland as a foreigner | Pankkitutka
highlights:
You can open a bank account in Finland as a foreigner, but the requirements depend on the bank and on whether you already have a Finnish personal identity code (henkilötunnus). The table below shows which banks in our data allow opening an account without one.

...

| Bank | Online opening with Finnish bank credentials | Without a Finnish personal ID | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S-Bank | Yes | Yes | Online or in the S-mobiili app if you have another Finnish bank's online banking credentials and a permanent address in the Population Information System (service in Finnish or Swedish only). Without a Finnish personal identity code you can apply at a service point with an ID document and an official proof of address, but you only get restricted online banking credentials that cannot be used for public e-services. |
| OP | Yes | - not available | You can become a customer online if you are an adult, have online banking credentials from a Finnish bank, are a citizen of an EEA country and have a permanent address and municipality of residence in Finland. Otherwise the customer relationship is opened at a branch by appointment. The possibility of opening an account without a Finnish personal identity code was not verified. |
| Nordea | Yes | Yes | Online if you are an adult living in Finland with a valid Finnish passport or ID card, another Finnish bank's online banking credentials and a Finnish phone number. People who have moved to Finland can open a customer relationship at a branch by appointment with an accepted ID document and proof of right of residence; Nordea says a Finnish personal identity code speeds things up and recommends getting one before applying. Service in Finnish, Swedish and English. |
| Danske Bank | Yes | - not available | You become a customer online with Finnish online banking credentials and a Finnish mobile phone number. If you do not have online banking credentials, are not an adult or do not live in Finland, the instruction is to contact customer service. Opening an account without a Finnish personal identity code was not verified. |
| Säästöpankki | No | - not available | The Säästöpankkiryhmä asks you to leave a contact request; the customer relationship and services are opened in a meeting at a branch or in an online video meeting. No self-service online account opening was found. Opening without a Finnish personal identity code was not verified. |
| POP Bank | No | - not available | You become a customer by booking a branch appointment or a POP Verkkohetki remote meeting; no self-service online account opening was found. Opening without a Finnish personal identity code was not verified. |
| Oma Säästöpankki | No | - not available | The customer relationship is opened in an online or branch meeting; no self-service online opening was found. OmaSp has been part of the S-Bank group since 7 October 2026, but its services continue unchanged in its own channels for now. Opening without a Finnish personal identity code was not verified. |
| Aktia | No | - not available | Everyday banking services (account, card and online bank) are opened by booking an appointment; switching banks can be arranged in a remote meeting. A child's account can be opened online with a junior power of attorney. Opening without a Finnish personal identity code was not verified. |
| Ålandsbanken | No | - not available | You become a customer by filling in a contact form, after which the bank contacts you and goes through your needs; services for minors require a branch visit with parents. No self-service online current account opening was found. Opening without a Finnish personal identity code was not verified. |
| Revolut | - not available | - not available | The account is opened in the Revolut app. Revolut Bank UAB is a bank licensed in Lithuania. Opening without a Finnish personal identity code and the identification method were not verified from Revolut's own pages in this review. |
| N26 | - not available | - not available | N26 states that it offers accounts to residents of Finland; the account is opened in the app. N26 has no Finland-specific site (n26.com/en-fi does not load); the EU site is used. Opening without a Finnish personal identity code was not verified. |
| bunq | - not available | - not available | The account is opened in the app. Finland is on bunq's list of supported countries for personal accounts; applicants must reside in one of these EEA countries. Opening without a Finnish personal identity code was not verified. |
| Wise | - not available | - not available | The account is opened online or in the app; Wise publishes card prices for residents of Finland. Wise is not a bank. Opening without a Finnish personal identity code was not verified. |

results.title: Opening a bank account  | Instructions | Studies Service | University of Helsinki
highlights:
Opening a bank account can be a lengthy process, often stretching over several months. You can speed it up by booking an appointment with your chosen bank already before leaving your home country, as waiting times can be significant. Please note that to open a bank account you need a Finnish personal identity code and a municipality of residence registered at the Digital and Population Data Services Agency. If you don't have those yet, make sure you take care of this first before your bank appointment.

...

1.

...

2. Bring the required documents to your first bank appointment. Standard documents include:

- Passport or national ID card (if you are an EU/EEA citizen);

...

- Finnish residence permit card or confirmation of an EU/EEA citizen’s residence registration;
- Certificate of student status at the University of Helsinki (you can download it from Sisu);
- Employment contract (if applicable).

...

NB! A Finnish ID-card is not mandatory to open a bank account or to obtain an online banking ID and non-Finnish citizens have the right to access basic banking services. This is endorsed by the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority, which states that "The bank can only refuse an electronic identification service if the customer does not have a personal identity code or if he or she has not been entered in the population register." Nevertheless, some banks might still demand a Finnish ID-card or a form from the Finnish police, but you can always try to convince them otherwise by referring to the page of the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority.

results.title: Opening a bank account can still be hard for foreigners | Yle
highlights:
Accessing banking services is most difficult for foreigners who do not have a passport from their former homeland. In cases in which a person's identity cannot be confirmed, he or she is issued an alien's passport or a refugee travel document. These documents contain a notation of the uncertainty of identity.

...

Difficulties have also been encountered by some people coming to Finland to work or as exchange students. An EU identity card is not always accepted and a bank may require a Finnish ID document. Jens Kremer, who moved to Finland from Germany two years ago, was able to use his German ID to open a bank account, access online banking services and set up a home savings account. When he went back at a later date to apply for a credit card, his bank had changed its policy and would not accept the same ID.

"I was told that since I don't have a Finnish identification document, I can't get a credit card, and my other banking facilities would be withdrawn," Kremer relates.

He filed a complaint with the National Discrimination Tribunal. The bank reacted by approving his credit card application and pledging to correct its practices.
